results.question: Turn my tenancy agreement into a move-in checklist

run.text: Here is a move-in checklist based on your tenancy agreement:

passages.name: Tenancy agreement.pdf
passages.content:
ACCESS, INSURANCE AND THE INVENTORY
11. Access. 11.1 The Landlord or their agent may enter the Property to inspect its condition
or carry out repairs at reasonable times of day, after giving at least 24 hours’ written
notice. 11.2 In an emergency, such as a fire, flood or gas leak, the Landlord or their agent
may enter without notice. 11.3 During the last two months of the tenancy the Landlord may
show the Property to prospective tenants or buyers at reasonable times, after giving the
same notice.
12. Insurance. 12.1 The Landlord insures the building and the Landlord’s furniture and
contents listed in the Inventory. 12.2 The Landlord’s insurance does not cover the Tenant’s
own belongings, and the Tenant is advised to take out contents insurance. 12.3 The Tenant
must not do anything that would make the Landlord’s insurance invalid or increase the
premium, and must tell the Landlord’s agent at once about any event that might lead to a
claim.
13. The Inventory. 13.1 The Inventory was prepared by an independent inventory clerk before
the start date, with dated photographs of each room. 13.2 The Tenant has seven days from the
start date to return the Inventory signed, with any comments about items that are missing or
in a worse condition than recorded. If the Tenant does not return it within that time, the
Inventory will be treated as accurate. 13.3 At the end of the tenancy the clerk will carry
out a check-out inspection, which the Tenant may attend.
14. Parking and storage. 14.1 No parking space comes with the Property. The Tenant may apply
to Bristol City Council for a residents’ parking permit at their own cost. 14.2 Bicycles may
be kept in the communal bike store, but not in the hallway or on the stairs. The Tenant must
not store anything in the communal areas.

passages.name: Tenancy agreement.pdf
passages.content:
RENT, DEPOSIT AND PAYMENTS
5. Rent. 5.1 The rent is 1,150 pounds per calendar month, payable in advance on the first
day of each month by standing order to the account the Landlord’s agent names in writing.
5.2 The first payment is due on or before the start date and covers the period from 1 March
2026 to 31 March 2026. 5.3 Rent is due whether or not the Landlord or its agent asks for it.
5.4 If any rent is unpaid for more than fourteen days after the date it was due, the Tenant
must pay interest on the unpaid amount at three per cent a year above the Bank of England
base rate, from the date it was due until the date it is paid. 5.5 The Landlord may not
charge any other fee for a late payment, and will not charge for a returned standing order
unless the Tenant cancelled it.
6. Deposit. 6.1 On signing this agreement the Tenant pays a deposit of 1,326 pounds, which
is no more than five weeks’ rent. 6.2 The Landlord will protect the deposit with the Deposit
Protection Service within 30 days of receiving it, and will give the Tenant the prescribed
information about the scheme within the same period. 6.3 The deposit is security for the
Tenant’s obligations under this agreement. It is not a payment of rent, and the Tenant may
not use it to pay the last month’s rent.
6.4 At the end of the tenancy the Landlord may deduct from the deposit the reasonable cost
of putting right any damage to the Property or its contents beyond fair wear and tear, any
unpaid rent, and the cost of replacing lost keys. 6.5 The Landlord must tell the Tenant of
any proposed deductions within ten days of the end of the tenancy and return the rest of the
deposit within ten days of the parties agreeing the amount. 6.6 If the parties cannot agree,
either of them may ask the scheme’s free dispute resolution service to decide.
6.7 Utilities and council tax. The Tenant pays for gas, electricity, water, broadband, the
television licence and council tax for the Property from the start date until the tenancy
ends, and must tell the suppliers and Bristol City Council when the tenancy starts and ends.

results.question: What are my deadlines in my employment contract?

run.text: Here are the deadlines and actionable requirements specified in your employment contract:

passages.name: Employment contract.pdf
passages.content:
HOURS, PROBATION AND NOTICE
7. Probation. 7.1 The first six months of your employment are a probation period. During
probation your manager will meet you at least monthly to review your progress. 7.2 The
Company may extend probation by up to three months if it needs more time to assess you, and
will tell you in writing before the original period ends. 7.3 During probation either you or
the Company may end your employment by giving one week’s notice in writing.
8. Hours of work. 8.1 Your normal working hours are 37.5 hours a week, Monday to Friday,
with an unpaid lunch break of one hour each day. 8.2 You may choose your start and finish
times, as long as you are available during the core hours of 10am to 4pm and work your full
hours each week. 8.3 You agree that the 48 hour average weekly limit in the Working Time
Regulations does not apply to you. You may withdraw this agreement by giving three months’
written notice.
9. Notice after probation. 9.1 After you complete probation, you must give the Company four
weeks’ written notice to end your employment. 9.2 After probation, the Company must give you
at least four weeks’ written notice to end your employment. Once you have five years of
continuous employment, the notice the Company must give you increases by one week for each
further complete year of employment, up to a maximum of twelve weeks. 9.3 Nothing in this
clause stops the Company from ending your employment without notice for gross misconduct.
9.4 The Company may decide to pay you basic salary in place of all or part of your notice
period. 9.5 During all or part of your notice period the Company may put you on garden
leave. While on garden leave you remain employed and paid, but you must not attend work or
contact clients or colleagues about work unless the Company asks you to, and you must not
start work for anyone else. 9.6 On your last day you must return all Company property,
documents and data, and delete any Company information held on your own devices.

passages.name: Employment contract.pdf
passages.content:
PAY AND BENEFITS
5. Salary. 5.1 Your salary is 68,500 pounds a year, paid in twelve equal instalments by bank
transfer on the 28th day of each month, or on the last working day before it if the 28th is
not a working day. 5.2 Your salary is reviewed each April, with any change taking effect
from 1 April. A review does not mean your salary will increase. 5.3 The Company may deduct
from your pay any money you owe it, including overpaid salary, unreturned equipment and any
holiday taken in excess of your entitlement when you leave.
5.4 You are not entitled to paid overtime. Your salary takes account of the occasional need
to work beyond your normal hours. 5.5 You are eligible for the Company’s discretionary
annual bonus scheme. Any bonus is worth up to ten per cent of your salary, depends on the
Company’s results and your own performance, and is paid in June. You must be employed and
not under notice on the payment date to receive a bonus.
6. Expenses. 6.1 The Company will repay reasonable expenses you incur while carrying out
your duties, in line with the expenses policy. 6.2 Claims must be submitted through the
expenses system with receipts within 60 days of the expense being incurred. Claims submitted
later may not be paid. 6.3 Travel between your home and your normal place of work is not a
business expense.
6.4 Pension. The Company will enrol you in its workplace pension scheme with Harrow Life in
line with automatic enrolment law. The Company contributes 5 per cent of your basic salary
and you contribute 4 per cent, by salary sacrifice unless you choose otherwise. You may opt
out of the scheme within one month of being enrolled. 6.5 Other benefits. After probation
you are eligible for private medical insurance for yourself, life assurance worth four times
your salary, and the cycle to work scheme. These benefits are provided under the rules of
each scheme, which may change.

passages.name: Employment contract.pdf
passages.content:
SICKNESS AND FAMILY LEAVE
13. Reporting sickness. 13.1 If you are unable to work because of sickness or injury, you
must tell your manager by phone or video call as soon as possible, and no later than 9.30am
on your first day of absence. A message or email is only acceptable if you cannot call. 13.2
You must keep your manager informed of how you are and when you expect to return. 13.3 For
absences of up to seven calendar days you must complete a self-certification form on the HR
system on the day you return to work. For absences of more than seven calendar days you must
provide a fit note from your doctor covering the whole of the absence.
14. Sick pay. 14.1 You are entitled to Statutory Sick Pay if you meet the conditions for it.
14.2 Once you have completed probation, the Company will also pay your full basic salary,
including any Statutory Sick Pay, for up to four weeks of sickness absence in any rolling
period of twelve months, and half of your basic salary for a further four weeks. 14.3
Company sick pay is discretionary and may be withheld if you do not follow the reporting
rules or if the absence results from a sport or activity done professionally.
14.4 The Company may ask you to see an occupational health adviser or a doctor it nominates,
at its expense, and you agree to the report being shared with the Company. 14.5 If you are
often absent or absent for a long time, the Company will meet you to discuss support and any
reasonable adjustments before taking any other step.
15. Family leave. 15.1 You are entitled to maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental
and parental bereavement leave and pay as set out in the law and in the family leave policy
in the Staff Handbook, which in some cases is more generous than the law. 15.2 You may take
reasonable unpaid time off to deal with an emergency involving a dependant. 15.3 You may
also take up to five days of paid carer’s leave a year after probation.

passages.name: Employment contract.pdf
passages.content:
HOLIDAYS
10. Holiday year and entitlement. 10.1 The holiday year runs from 1 January to 31 December.
10.2 You are entitled to 25 days of paid holiday in each holiday year, in addition to the
eight usual bank holidays in England. If you work part-time, your entitlement is reduced in
proportion. 10.3 After three complete years of employment, your holiday entitlement
increases to 27 days, and after five complete years to 28 days. 10.4 In the holiday year in
which your employment starts or ends, your entitlement is worked out in proportion to the
part of the year you are employed, rounded up to the nearest half day.
11. Booking holiday. 11.1 You must book holiday through the HR system and have it approved
by your manager before making any travel arrangements. 11.2 You must give at least twice as
much notice as the length of the holiday you want to take, and at least two weeks’ notice
for any holiday of more than five days. 11.3 You may not take more than ten working days in
a row without the approval of your director. 11.4 The Company closes between Christmas and
New Year and you must keep three days of your entitlement for that period.
12. Carrying holiday over. 12.1 You should take all of your holiday in the holiday year in
which it is earned. 12.2 You may carry over up to five days of unused holiday into the next
holiday year, but you must take them by 31 March of that year or they will be lost. 12.3 If
you could not take holiday because of sickness or family leave, you may carry over the
holiday you were unable to take, and must use it within eighteen months of the end of the
year in which it was earned.
12.4 Holiday on leaving. When your employment ends you will be paid for any holiday you have
earned in that year but not taken. If you have taken more holiday than you earned, the
Company will deduct the excess from your final pay. Apart from this, the Company does not
pay in place of untaken holiday. 12.5 The Company may ask you to take any remaining holiday
during your notice period.

run.text: Here are your coursework tasks and deadlines based on the syllabus:

passages.name: Course syllabus.pdf
passages.content:
DATA2041 APPLIED DATA VISUALISATION: MODULE HANDBOOK, AUTUMN 2026
School of Computing, University of Eastbridge. Module leader: Dr Imogen Achterberg
(i.achterberg@eastbridge.example). Teaching runs for eleven weeks from Monday 28 September
2026. Lectures are on Mondays at 10am in the Hollins Building, room 2.14, and lab sessions
are on Thursdays at 2pm in the Ada Lab.
1. Aims. 1.1 The module teaches you to design charts and dashboards that are accurate,
accessible and honest about uncertainty. 1.2 You will work with real public datasets in
Python and present your findings to a non-specialist audience.
2. Attendance. 2.1 You are expected to attend every lecture and lab. 2.2 If you miss a lab,
you must catch up on the lab exercise before the next lab session, using the notes on the
module page. 2.3 If you will miss more than two consecutive weeks, you must tell the module
leader by email.
3. Reading. 3.1 Before the first lecture, read chapters 1 and 2 of the set text,
Fundamentals of Honest Charts. 3.2 Each week’s reading is listed on the module page and
should be done before that week’s lecture.
4. Assessment. 4.1 Coursework 1 is a project proposal of no more than 800 words, worth 10
per cent of the module mark. You must submit it through the coursework portal by 5pm on
Friday 16 October 2026. 4.2 Coursework 2 is a draft dashboard with a short write-up, worth
20 per cent. You must submit the draft through the portal by 5pm on Friday 6 November 2026.
4.3 After the draft deadline you will be sent two classmates’ drafts to review. You must
submit both peer reviews within seven days of receiving them. Peer reviews are not marked
but are required to pass the module.
4.4 The final project, worth 50 per cent, is a finished dashboard with a report of no more
than 2,500 words. You must hand it in through the portal by 5pm on Friday 11 December 2026.
